source.title: Structural Graph Probing of Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Hao-Yu He; Yue Zhuo; Yu Zheng; Qi R. Wang

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies correlation topology and interventions on selected neurons in vision-language models, but it does not test any listed claim version about neuron poles, explanation accuracy, or explanatory sufficiency.
record.gate_note: The paper reports behavioral effects of interventions on topology-selected neurons and neuron pairs. These results concern neuron influence, but do not measure the claim versions’ proposed one-job share, explanation prediction accuracy, or attribution-graph sufficiency. The probing and hallucination-prediction results concern graph representations, not the claim’s neuron explanations.
record.test_reason: The study builds neuron-correlation graphs in VLMs, probes them, and ablates or perturbs topology-selected hub neurons and edges. It never assigns explanations or jobs to individual neurons. It does not score explanations against activations or build attribution graphs, so no version's measure is reported. Its discussion argues for population-level units rather than independently interpretable neurons. That is a framing, not a result on V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that within-layer neuron-correlation topology carries recoverable behavioural signal. They also find that cross-modal structure consolidates with depth around recurrent hub neurons, and that perturbing these hubs substantially changes model output. They frame topology as an intermediate interpretability scale. Their discussion suggests multimodal reasoning is better seen as emergent from neural populations than as a sum of independently interpretable components. That is a framing that leans against neuron-level sufficiency, but it is not tested against any version.
record.recipe_differences: The study constructs neuron-correlation graphs and probes or intervenes on topology-defined hubs; it does not use the original studies’ neuron-pole explanation or explanation-scoring methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The strongest ablation effect occurs at different layers by model: around layer 11 for InternVL3-1B and layer 0 for Qwen2.5-VL-3B. The selected edge interventions have different effects: identical partner activity causes little degradation, random replacement a moderate decline, and opposite activity the largest decline.

fits_no_version.finding: Zeroing the top 1% of neurons by correlation-graph degree drops VLM accuracy more than activation-based or random selection. On Qwen2.5-VL-3B layer 0 the drop reaches about 86 points on CLEVR counting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correlation-graph hub neurons are more behaviourally influential than activation-magnitude-selected neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: On the strongest graph edge, replacing one endpoint with its negated partner activation degrades accuracy most; an identical copy barely changes it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The sign alignment of coupled neuron pairs matters for VLM task performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling hub-neuron activations up or down degrades performance roughly symmetrically.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Topology-defined hubs operate within a narrow functional range.

record.problems: The study does not test whether neuron explanations generalize to new activations or whether neurons suffice as explanatory units. The intervention figures contain plotted values whose exact mappings are not stated in the text; the relevant qualitative comparisons are reported in prose.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately described claim-relevant results were left out. Graph-probe benchmark scores, graph alignment, hub recurrence, and hallucination classification were not extracted as rows because they do not measure a listed claim version or the intervention findings summarized under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: All of it: no per-neuron job counts in Qwen3-32B or any other model.
All of it: no neuron interpretability shares across models or scale.
All of it: no InceptionV1 or polysemantic-example analysis.
All of it: no comparison of interpretable-neuron share across architectures or tools.
All of it: no neuron-level attribution graphs and no replacement-model comparison. The correlation graphs are not circuits.
All of it: no neuron explanations are tested for activation prediction.
All of it: no simulation-based explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: Relation could arguably stay 'discusses' because the discussion questions individual neurons as explanatory units, but no result bears on V1–V7. Rows r1–r8 omitted the plotted numeric deltas visible in Figures 6 and 7. Rows r9–r12 mislabel activation scaling as weight_edit. The study evaluates its own method throughout.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron-pole job counts, including the one-job, two-job, and not-understood shares.
Neuron-pole shares across model families, architectures, and scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose, and recursive generalization.
Interpretability shares across architectures, tools, or regularization settings.
Attribution graphs, explanatory sufficiency, trained replacement models, and reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict new activations.
Automated simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

conditions.value: TDIUC and CLEVR; color and counting
